title: MSBuild spawns a suspicious child process
description: Detects MSBuild creating a selected command, script or signed proxy-execution process.

hypothesis.summary: An adversary may execute inline or embedded code through MSBuild and create a command, script or proxy-execution child process.
hypothesis.rationale: MITRE documents MSBuild proxy execution and recommends monitoring unusual child-process behavior; Microsoft lists MSBuild among applications that can bypass application-control policies if allowed. A bounded child list is more useful than alerting on every developer build.
hypothesis.detection_goal: Identify selected command, script and signed proxy-execution processes directly created by MSBuild while leaving expected compiler children, unrelated parent processes and incomplete events unmatched.

data_sources.name: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint process events

triage.summary: Treat the behavior as tuning-required until the build project and spawned tool are explained; developer systems and build agents can create legitimate command children.
steps: Review the child command, MSBuild parent command, project file, account, device role, working paths and signer context.
Inspect the project or inline task for embedded code and correlate network activity, file writes, persistence and follow-on processes.
Confirm the build with the repository and pipeline owner; scope any exception to a reviewed project, runner and command pattern rather than MSBuild globally.
false_positives: Approved build scripts, custom tasks or CI jobs that intentionally invoke command or script interpreters
Developer tooling that legitimately launches one of the selected signed Windows utilities from MSBuild

validation.expected_outcome: Match selected command, script or proxy-execution children directly spawned by MSBuild; do not match normal compiler children, another parent or missing parent context.
